links.outcome: LLM performance on hospital medication-safety scenarios (F1, sensitivity, specificity) across 40 models
links.effect: F1 78.5%–92.3%, accuracy 65.4%–89.8%, sensitivity 81.4%–100.0%, specificity 6.1%–81.8%; three models had 100% sensitivity but below 25% specificity, like an always-alert classifier.
links.quote: Headline binary performance on the full benchmark spans a wide range across the 40 models: F1 78.5%–92.3%, accuracy 65.4%–89.8%, sensitivity 81.4%–100.0%, specificity 6.1%–81.8%.

links.outcome: LLM detection of unsafe medication orders across safety categories
links.effect: Sensitivity 81.4%–100.0% across 40 models, but specificity 6.1%–81.8%; three models saturated sensitivity at 100% with under 25% specificity.
links.quote: three models saturate sensitivity at 100% but fall below 25% specificity, indistinguishable from a naive always-alert classifier.

unlisted_practices: Tiered benchmark framework separating discrimination, operational, and attribution performance for medication-safety classifiers
Reporting specificity alongside sensitivity to detect always-alert classifiers

screen.reason: The study introduces and runs an automated benchmark (PsiBench) evaluating 40 large language models on hospital medication safety scenarios; it tests model performance but does not compare outcomes with and without a specific deployment safeguard or practice.
